opportunities.observation: The qualified M384 branch is greedy and the first downstream consumer needs only 384 post-softcap lowest-ID argmax values before request-owned tree acceptance.
opportunities.evidence_scope: Gemma 4 31B pinned SGLang v0.5.13, TP1, c32 NGRAM, 12 target rows/request, M384, temperature zero, H200 SM90a
opportunities.phase: target verification output head through first KV commit
opportunities.resource_signature: 1.082331758592 TFLOP, 2.625 GiB tied weight, 192 MiB BF16 output, 384 MiB FP32 logits
competing_explanations: The stock GEMM/softcap/argmax intermediates may remain in cache and cost little.
Fused epilogue register/shared-memory pressure may slow the output head.
The second-stage reduction may cost more than avoided stores.
The boundary may be too small end to end despite a positive component.
opportunities.mechanism: BM64xBN256 BF16 output-head tiles emit only per-row post-softcap (value,id) partials; 32 request reducers finish argmax and tree greedy acceptance.
opportunities.modifiable_fraction: All full-logit interface traffic; none of the 1.082331758592 TFLOP output-head compute.
opportunities.upper_bound: 2,006,971,392 logical bytes and three source-visible operations per full M384 wave; 0.41811904 ms peak-HBM zero-cache time scale.
opportunities.falsifier: Any selected-token/acceptance/KV mismatch, illegal resource use, spills, nonpositive component latency, or no L2/DRAM reduction.
opportunities.next_measurement: Alternating exact H200 stock/candidate M384 producer-to-acceptance component with bitwise state oracle and minimal counters.
opportunities.expected_information_per_dollar: High only if piggybacked on an already-authorized retained H200; no spend is authorized here.

opportunities.observation: One-request slabs bound FP32 logits to 32 MiB while retaining exact stock consumers.
opportunities.evidence_scope: Same M384 geometry and pinned runtime
opportunities.resource_signature: 12 full vocabulary GEMMs and 33,822,867,456 logical weight bytes
competing_explanations: A persistent-weight kernel might retain some head tiles across slabs.
opportunities.mechanism: Materialize one request's 12 rows, run stock acceptance, and repeat.
opportunities.falsifier: The compulsory weight reread exceeds the removed logit traffic even at ideal HBM.
opportunities.next_measurement: None; closed analytically unless a future persistent head proves cross-slab weight residency.

opportunities.observation: Sampled target verification constructs full target_probs and draft_probs, but acceptance reads sparse draft probabilities plus one final row.
opportunities.evidence_scope: Non-greedy NGRAM target verification and optional runtime features
opportunities.resource_signature: Global top-p ordering, arbitrary custom row processors, and potentially unbounded top-logprob output
competing_explanations: Finite top-k could admit a bounded heap fast path.
A multi-pass external-memory sort could reduce peak workspace but not global semantic dependence.
opportunities.mechanism: Stream probabilities and retain only acceptance scalars/final-row state.
opportunities.falsifier: Exact top-p/custom/top-logprob behavior cannot be represented by bounded constant row state for all legal inputs.
opportunities.next_measurement: None for the qualified greedy endpoint; keep exact materialized fallback. A separately scoped finite-top-k-only endpoint could reopen.
